---
title: "Getting Started"
---

MLPerf EDU runs on a laptop. You need Python 3.10+ and
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). No GPU is required; Apple MPS and CUDA are
used automatically when present.

## Install

The suite is installed with uv, either as a tool or from a source checkout.

**As a tool (recommended for running benchmarks):**

```bash
uv tool install mlperf-edu
mlperf doctor
```

**From a source checkout (recommended for coursework and development):**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book.git
cd cs249r_book/mlperf-edu
uv sync --extra dev
uv run mlperf doctor
```

`mlperf doctor` checks Python, PyTorch, the accelerator, the data and model
caches, and the workload registry. Every row should read `ok` or `optional`
before you continue.

## First Run

```bash
mlperf init --profile min
```

`init` prepares local caches and runs the minimum representative path, one
small workload from each suite. On a recent laptop the whole pass takes well
under a minute. Each workload writes four artifacts into `submissions/`:

| **Artifact** | **What it is** |
|:---|:---|
| `<workload>_min_report.json` | Full machine-readable result |
| `<workload>_min_report.html` | Human-readable report (open in a browser) |
| `<workload>_min_report.csv` | Spreadsheet-friendly metrics |
| `<workload>_min.provd.json` | Provenance artifact (hashes, fingerprints) |

## Explore the Registry

```bash
mlperf list                          # all workloads
mlperf list --suite slm              # one suite
mlperf show nanogpt-train            # one workload's full contract
mlperf info --dataset tinyshakespeare
mlperf info --model smollm2-135m
```

The same information is browsable on this site under
[Benchmarks](benchmarks/index.qmd); those pages are generated from the same
registry the CLI reads.

## Run a Real Benchmark

```bash
mlperf fetch --workload nanogpt-train --profile max
mlperf run --workload nanogpt-train --profile max --open-report
```

`fetch` downloads and verifies assets ahead of time so the measured run is
clean. `run` executes the benchmark and writes reports; `--open-report` opens
the HTML report when the run finishes.

Continue with the [running guide](guide/running.qmd) for profiles, suite
selection, and power measurement, or jump straight to a
[benchmark page](benchmarks/index.qmd) for copy-paste commands per workload.
